_about: Which llama.cpp backend runs on which GPU, for shared/forge_gpu.py and forge_link.py (Relay task 524). backends: tried in order, the first one that suits a device and has a build wins. suits: vendors (nvidia, amd, intel, other) and kinds (discrete, integrated) it is meant for; prefer_over_vulkan false means it is only used when Emerson asks for it by name (--backend), true means it wins over Vulkan when its build is there. build: the official ggml-org/llama.cpp release asset per OS ({build} is the build number, such as b11980); both PCs of a split need the same build. memory: how much of a device's free memory a model may take. integrated: an iGPU shares the system RAM, so it gets share_of_free of what is free, and never more than leaves keep_ram_mb of RAM free (the same 4096 MB forge_ram's model_load rule keeps). discrete: keep_free_mb stays free for the desktop and other apps. cpu: the layers left on the CPU keep keep_ram_mb of RAM free too. overhead: what a model needs beyond its weights, as a fraction of the weights plus fixed MB for the KV cache and compute buffers at the default context.

backends.name: CUDA
backends.why: NVIDIA's own compute path; the fastest on NVIDIA cards

backends.name: ROCm (HIP)
backends.why: AMD's compute path: faster prompt reading on supported Radeon RX 6000/7000/9000 cards, but it needs a supported card and driver stack, so Vulkan stays the default

backends.name: SYCL (oneAPI)
backends.why: Intel's compute path for Arc cards: faster prompt reading there, but it needs the oneAPI runtime, so Vulkan stays the default

backends.name: Vulkan
backends.why: works on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel cards and on integrated graphics with the normal graphics driver

backends.name: CPU
backends.why: the last resort: no graphics card llama.cpp can use
